Case built for teaching: the underlying CT is real (public archive) and has no lesions; the lesions were added by computer with the noise of the original image. The realism is good but simplified: no histology, the outcome is the one set in the simulation.
Metastases from colorectal carcinoma are generally hypovascular: hypodense in the portal phase, often with a denser peripheral rim (viable tumor and compressed parenchyma) and a more hypodense center. They must be counted and assigned to segments because they determine resectability; MRI with hepatospecific contrast and diffusion finds more small lesions than CT.
Not all hypodense lesions in an oncologic patient are metastases: cysts have water density and well-defined margins; below 1 cm many lesions remain uncharacterizable on CT.
Paziente con tumore del colon: conta le: Patient with colon cancer: count the liver lesions and distinguish cysts (water density) from metastases (rim, solid density).
